experiment: E215 (rl_67m), cell P2.41 stage 1: what the 67M base model already samples, per behaviour with a programmed reward
filed: 2026-11-19, before any GPU run of this code; descriptive (user, 2026-11-19, task file)

settings.temperature_source: the brief (2026-11-19): 16 sampled tokens at temperature 1
settings.n_prompts_source: chosen so a rate of 0.2 has a standard error near 0.02 to 0.03 over prompts (card); the dry run found 256 eligible prompts for every behaviour

rule_text: commute.rl_tasks.select. A behaviour is eligible with at least 128 prompts read, usable when also 0.05 <= rate <= 0.5 (ends included). Pick 1: the usable behaviour whose rate is nearest 0.2 (distance rounded to 1e-9, so 0.15 and 0.25 tie); pick 2: the nearest usable one of a different family. Ties go to the earlier in the filed order (commute.rl_tasks.BEHAVIOURS: lower, french_fr, french_en, german_de, german_en, close_paren, close_quote, repeat, counting, end_sentence, sports, business, emoticon). Anchor: the eligible behaviour of lowest rate strictly under 0.01, ties to the earlier; none if no rate is under 0.01 (reported, no stop). Fewer than two picks: stop and report, before any training. Edge cases run 2026-11-19 on the dry-run script: fewer than two usable, none usable, the 0.15/0.25 tie, two usable of one family only, band ends, two anchors tied at 0, no anchor, an anchor at exactly 0.01, too few prompts; each gave the stated result

definitions.rate: the share of the 256 x 8 sampled continuations that earn the reward, at W0, temperature 1, 16 tokens after a 64-token held-out prompt (21 tokens for emoticon windows)
definitions.sd_over_prompts: the population sd over prompts of each prompt's mean reward over its 8 samples; se = sd / sqrt(256)
definitions.mixed_share: the share of prompts whose 8 samples hold both a 0 and a 1: the prompts a group-baseline policy gradient learns from
definitions.true_rate: the reward on the text's own next 16 tokens: the positive control that the reward program sees the behaviour where the text shows it
definitions.kl_from_base: mean over every position of the 64 held-out Pile val rows 0-63 (512 tokens each) of KL(W0's next-token distribution || W0 + dW's), fp32 per position, float64 sum: the output change stage 2 stops every arm at

control.stage 0, first and alone: kl_from_base at a zero update reads exactly 0.0, and at a Gaussian update of relative size 0.01 per matrix reads above 0; else stop
control.stage 0, reward program: the reward on the texts' own continuations: counting exactly 1.0, French Wikipedia read as French >= 0.8, German Wikipedia read as German >= 0.7, English Pile read as French or German <= 0.05; else stop. The dry run (CPU, the same code and rows) read 1.0, 0.848, 0.758, 0.0, 0.004, so the job is expected to reproduce those exactly

expected_at_W0.kl_random: above 0, about 1e-4 to 1e-2 nats per token (a guess; only the sign is a stop)

rate.emoticon: 0.005 to 0.03 (E1's W0 P(o) at the trigger, 0.011)

expected_at_W0.picks: two of lower, end_sentence and repeat (low confidence on which); anchor french_en (rate 0, ties german_en and comes first)
expected_at_W0.sample_seconds_per_batch: 0.2 to 2 s for 256 sequences x 16 tokens on an L40 (a guess; measured here for stage 2)
